title: 2010 HMMT February Guts Problem 2
statement: Suppose that \(x, y\), and \(z\) are non-negative real numbers such that \(x+y+z=1\). What is the maximum possible value of \(x+y^{2}+z^{3}\) ?

solutions.text: 1 Since \(0 \leq y, z \leq 1\), we have \(y^{2} \leq y\) and \(z^{3} \leq z\). Therefore \(x+y^{2}+z^{3} \leq x+y+z=1\). We can get \(x+y^{2}+z^{3}=1\) by setting \((x, y, z)=(1,0,0)\).
